messages.author: 1a67aeb93edceb01
messages.subject: Managing source code
parts:
I'm just getting started with shiny and understand all required source files need to be in the application directory. Fine, but what if your app uses some function(s) you've defined in file(s) in another directory, perhaps under git control, for example. In a "traditional" software model, a Makefile would handle compiling and linking; perhaps your other function is compiled to a library that is linked to by your GUI.

Does anyone have any recommendations for handling this in a neat way with R/shiny? Taking a copy of your function code to put in your shiny app directory feels kludgy and means it's either no longer version controlled or gets version controlled separately from its original. Symlink? This would work locally, but would the shiny deployment pull in, and deploy, the required file, or would you end up with a broken link? Good practice? Ideas?

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: Managing source code
parts:
A couple of ideas here:

You could bundle your shared code as a package (this is the standard way to share code in R). shinyapps.io supports installing packages from private GitHub repositories. Your app would then load the shared code like any other package using library().

Alternatively, you could use git submodules. For example if you have a git repo called "my-library", you can use a git submodule to checkout "my-library" into your project's git repository. The advantages of submodules vs copying the files is that you can manage the two projects separately, but still share the code (think of the submodule as a pointer to another repository).

More on submodules:
https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Submodules

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: Managing source code
parts:
Thanks Andy, good points there.

I had seen a shiny tutorial mention the option to specify required packages (package.require() or something when deploying to shinyapps.io?). I didn't realise shinyapps.io could actually go and install a remote package, so that's interesting to bear in mind. My code isn't at the point of becoming a package.

I like the git submodule approach, although I'd be specifying a local path rather than URL to a remote repository (for now).
I see the submodule approach would create a subdirectory. So how would you integrate that into the shiny app? I'm starting with a simple app and following the guideline/requirement of "all your R files in the app directory". In fact, all R code is in ui.R and server.R thus far. Just as you can specify "library(xxx)" in these files, can you also run "source('./submodule/Rsrc.R')"? And if you deployed it, would the deploy utility know to include ./submodule/Rsrc.R?
(I suspect this is a similar question/answer to if I created a symlink to Rsrc.R in the app directory) - would the deploy utility know to include the target file in the package?

Regards,
Guy

messages.author: f2961c15f7afbca6
messages.subject: Re: Managing source code
parts:
Another consideration (depending on scope of the project) is to just create your own library that wraps up everything. It's not that much more work, provides consistent organization so can easily be shared across users (eg I know where to look for tests etc). The for setup you can easily just do a dependency check by either commit hash or library version. So your app becomes as easy as library(<app-lib>). Combine this with packrat if you want even finer grained portability for deployments.

Maybe its my lack of ever needing a true make file, but it seems that much of the functionality you mentioned (eg compilation/linking) doesn't really hold for R code since you aren't compiling it, and there aren't central places where people have Rscripts laying around to link in the same sense that you'd be linking to say a boost library. Any linking you do need to do (eg for Rcpp) could be done upon package installation for the overall system.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Managing source code
parts: Just as you can specify "library(xxx)" in these files, can you also run "source('./submodule/Rsrc.R')"?
Yes, though you often want to do source("./submodule/Rsrc.R", local = TRUE) unless you want Rsrc.R to be evaluated in the global environment (which is the default behavior).
And if you deployed it, would the deploy utility know to include ./submodule/Rsrc.R?
Also yes--the deploy utility will grab the entire directory by default.
